outcome: Give university cio / academic program director a governed method to improve time to licensed source retrieval using library holdings, subscriptions and researcher inquiries, with final decisions…
overview: Library Research Discovery with Licensing addresses staff search multiple approved sources manually and struggle to preserve permissions and version context in education and research operations. The first proof of value uses library holdings, subscriptions and researcher inquiries. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is time to licensed source retrieval, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: library holdings, subscriptions and researcher inquiries; define time to licensed source retrieval and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from University CIO / Academic Program Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including golden question set with prompt-injection and authorization tests.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for time to licensed source retrieval
